narrative: A PR that tagged every CromError raise with a Reason slug drew 42 findings over four rounds. Almost all were real: test-coverage gaps where the new .reason was never asserted, plus a few genuine misclassifications (stranger-on-port, the parse_layer downgrade, -1743, the PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED overreach, _load's OSError, reserved switches, chrome-profile traversal). Most findings after round 0 were the agent's own incomplete sweeps: it pinned only the files each round named, dropped items the reviewer listed by name, and in F19 replied Fixed for plan items that never landed. Every later round also carried at least one finding on original code (F23/F24, F38, F40), so no whole round was strictly avoidable, but 22 of the 26 post-round-0 findings trace back to incomplete earlier fixes.
guidance_observations: The agent set a sound dosing rule (pin confusable pairs) in round 0 but applied it only to files the reviewer named, and conceded as much in round 1; applying the rule once across the whole diff would have collapsed rounds 1-3 to a handful of findings.
Twice (F9→F21 and F19→F30/F31) a `Fixed in <sha>` reply covered plan items absent from the named commit; diffing the plan against the commit before replying would have caught both.

The PR introduced a per-site classification with no per-site assertions at all; a PR adding an enum tag at N raise sites should ship with a check that every member appears in at least one test assertion.

The agent's corrections of reviewer mechanics were accurate and kept vacuous tests out: Path.home vs os.path.expanduser (F26), the rmtree route rewrapped before reaching _errno_reason (F13), and one _profiles_table raise rather than three (F41).
